basis: Defined by destructive osteolysis; no additional organ involvement applies across this umbrella.
Malignant thyroid-type tissue within an ovarian teratoma; ovarian origin is outside the axes. Thyrotoxicosis is uncommon and does not establish common endocrine dysfunction.
Skeletal anomalies, cutis laxa and intellectual disability define the syndrome; cardiac anomalies, including PDA and cardiomegaly, occur in 30-79%.
Neuroendocrine neoplasm defined by atypical carcinoid histology; the supplied definition specifies no anatomical site, so no pulmonary or gastrointestinal site is assumed.
Generalized follicular keratosis, alopecia and cerebral atrophy define the syndrome. Proportionate dwarfism alone does not establish skeletal or endocrine pathology.
Lysosomal glycogen storage directly damages skeletal and respiratory muscles. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness rather than intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Fungal infection directly involves skin, hair or nails.
Severe developmental epileptic encephalopathy; genu valgum occurs in 4/12 (~33%). Constipation and feeding difficulty do not establish direct gastrointestinal damage.
Defined by amyloid deposition in brain parenchyma and cerebral vessel walls, producing neurodegeneration and cerebral angiopathy.
An age-dependent epilepsy syndrome; spontaneous remission does not change its neurologic location.
Inherited glomerular disease causing proteinuria and commonly chronic kidney failure; familial steroid resistance does not establish an immune mechanism.
Marrow/blood lymphoblast malignancy within the lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma spectrum; hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly occurs in roughly 30-60%.
Ancestors identify a conjunctival pterygium extending centrally across the ocular surface.
Skeletal dysplasia and hearing loss define it. Urinary obstruction/hydronephrosis and subglottic stenosis each occur in 30-79%; cardiac anomalies omitted because of the four-axis cap.
A primary central nervous system glial neoplasm.
Characteristic molar root abnormalities and juvenile glaucoma define the recognized syndrome; hypotrichosis and digital anomalies have insufficient frequency evidence.
Cancer of the tonsillar ring in the pharynx, included in the pulmonary axis. The concept does not specify lymphoma.
Retinal neovascular disease directly threatens vision; diabetes is the underlying separately diagnosed disease rather than an additional damaged organ here.
Generalized dystonia with central and peripheral neurologic dysfunction; vocal cord structural abnormalities occur in 30-79%, supporting direct laryngeal involvement.
Pericardial fibrosis and thickening directly restrict cardiac filling; no specific infectious or autoimmune cause is established.
Rickettsia felis infection; rash is transient, while neurologic dysfunction and pulmonary compromise are explicitly rare.
Intellectual disability and eye abnormalities are defining features. Unspecified dwarfism does not establish a skeletal lesion or an endocrine disorder.
Joint laxity, pectus carinatum and genu valgum define skeletal involvement; facial appearance alone does not establish damage to another axis.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss occurs in 8/9 patients; cochlear nerve hypoplasia remains within the hearing axis.
B-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma; hepatic leukemic infiltration occurs in roughly 30-60% of ALL overall, although PAX5 P80R-specific frequency is uncertain.
